formal: I began searching for a new position because of the manner in which my manager treats the team, and I subsequently received an offer from another company. When I informed my current employer, they offered me a 15% raise in order to remain; however, the manager will not change. My plan is to accept the counteroffer and decline the other position. I have compared the raise with the outside offer on the criteria that matter to me, and I have reached this decision. I rarely bring career decisions of this kind to you, so asking about this matter is unusual for me. What is your opinion?

When I told my current company about that offer, they came back and offered me a 15% raise to stay, but the manager stays the same, so that part isn't changing. The plan, then, is to take the counteroffer and turn the other job down. I have weighed the raise against the outside offer on the points that count for me, and having done that, I decided on this plan. I should also say that I rarely bring career choices like this to you, so asking about it is unusual for me. Given all of that, what's your view?
